data.goal: Give a tester one drag gesture on the live Android mirror that freezes the exact frame they saw the bug in, boxes it, numbers it and opens a focused place to describe it — with the box stored in device screenshot pixels so it stays correct across host density, window resize and panel resize. New code is deliberately tiny: one pure geometry function, one kit molecule (the dim scrim), two defaulted kit parameters, and six Orbit intents. Everything visible is assembled from shipped, previewed kit components.
data.problemStatement: F-1 (shell) and F-2 (device discovery + live mirror) deliver a live mirror with no way to mark anything on it — a tester can only describe a bug in prose or attach a raw screenshot, which is exactly what this product exists to replace. rectify-poc proved the drag-box interaction is feasible but also documented a silent density-conversion bug: pointer events and the composable's own layout are in raw screen pixels, while Modifier.offset/size take Dp which Compose multiplies by density again, so every drawn rectangle lands `density`x from the cursor (2x on this Retina host). That bug corrupts every annotation's anchor and no existing test would catch it. Separately, F-1 shipped three slots explicitly reserved for this feature — ShellToolbar.stagedCounter, ShellToolbar.clearAction and SidePanelFrame's Notes tab — as inert stubs, and StatusIndicatorState.Frozen shipped with zero callers. This spec closes the coordinate hole and fills the reserved slots.
data.highLevelDescription: Four layers, no new Gradle module, no new catalog entry, no persistence. (1) GEOMETRY — a new internal, pure, non-Composable FrameGeometry in presentation-feature-mirror/core/geometry/, unit-tested BEFORE any UI exists. Pointer offsets from pointerInput and the frame box size from onSizeChanged are in the SAME pixel space, so `devicePx = pointerPx / frameBoxPx * deviceSize` contains no density at all; density applies in exactly one place, converting back out for rendering. (2) STATE — MirrorUiState gains `frozen: FrozenFrame?` holding a List<StagedAnnotation> and a selectedIndex; the frozen ImageBitmap itself goes on a second StateFlow beside `frame`, with the reducer storing only its IntSize. Annotations belong IN reduced state for the exact inverse of F-2's reason for keeping frames out: they are a handful of small value-equal records mutated by discrete user actions and read simultaneously by three consumers (toolbar badge, Notes tab, stage marks), whereas frames are identity-compared blobs arriving ten times a second. (3) FREEZE — a render-path switch only. sessionDeviceId and F-2's flatMapLatest capture gate are never touched, so Resume Live costs no new adb session and no first-frame latency; drag-in-progress offsets live in composable `remember` and never enter Orbit. (4) UI — assemble from AnnotationMark, Ruler, CommentPopover, AnnotationPopover, AnnotationRow, CounterBadge, StatusIndicatorState.Frozen and AppButton; author exactly one new kit molecule (AnnotationOverlay = scrim via clipPath(ClipOp.Difference) + one AnnotationMark per rect) and add two source-compatible defaulted parameters to shipped kit components. FR-9's gutter is an in-stage right-edge column, not the Notes tab, because FR-28 already fills that tab.

assumptions: AS-10: Manual/dev verification happens at host density 2.0 (Retina, per F-1's T-12 probe), but FrameGeometry takes density as a parameter rather than hardcoding 2.0.
AS-11: Exactly one frozen frame and its staged-annotation set exist in memory at a time within this spec's scope; multi-frame capture history is F-8's.
AS-12: The mirrored device's screen does not rotate or change resolution mid-annotation-session; handling that is out of scope.

AS-13: Clicking the toolbar's clearAction empties the staged list without a confirmation dialog — a direct, reversible-by-redrawing action, not a destructive-confirm flow, consistent with the toolbar's existing design.

AS-14 (plan): presentation-feature-mirror's build.gradle.kts needs NO edit. It already declares projects.presentationCoreUi, projects.presentationCoreLocalisation, projects.presentationCoreStyling, compose.material3 and libs.kotlinx.coroutines.test, and FeatureConventionPlugin already wires kotlin-test into commonTest. Verified by reading both files — this is the class of omission that bit F-2's draft plan.

AS-16 (plan): MirrorHost's and MirrorStageContent's PUBLIC signatures do not change. MirrorHost internally computes displayFrame = frozenFrame ?: frame and passes the single bitmap it already passes, so RectifyShellContent's parameter list and every existing call site stay source-compatible.

constraints.text: No literal Color(0x...), no raw .dp at a call site, no hardcoded TextStyle. Every invented value (scrim alpha, gutter width, Resume Live inset, minimum drag size, nominal popover bounds) is a named private file-top constant with a KDoc rationale — the pattern MirrorContent.kt's NoticeMaxWidth and the kit's own geometry blocks already use — or a new Theme token. Per .claude/rules/design-tokens.md.

A commonTest backtick test name containing a comma, apostrophe or colon compiles on the JVM and fails compileTestKotlinIosArm64 with 'Name contains illegal characters'. This already broke the repo once in F-1. Plain camelCase test names only, no backticks at all in new tests.

presentation-core-ui takes no dependency on presentation-core-localisation. AnnotationOverlay and every other kit-level change takes copy as a parameter with an English default; the feature module supplies stringResource().

presentation-core-ui enforces strict atom -> molecule -> organism layering. AnnotationOverlay lives in molecule/annotation/ and imports AnnotationMark (atom) only — never CommentPopover (organism). Popover placement and leader-line routing stay with the feature-module host.

Orbit MVI four-file convention for presentation-feature-mirror, with the module's two documented deviations intact (MirrorHost not MirrorScreen; no pixels in reduced state). The no-pixels rule extends to the frozen bitmap: it goes on a StateFlow beside frame, never into MirrorUiState.

core/ holds internal declarations only; source/ holds the public API. FrameGeometry, AnnotationFormat and popoverCrowding are internal and live under core/; StagedAnnotation / DeviceRect / FrozenFrame are public contract types and live in source/mirror/MirrorContract.kt. explicitApi() is enforced repo-wide: every public declaration needs an explicit visibility modifier and return type.

FrameGeometry is internal, pure, has no @Composable and no ViewModel side effects — the single code path for every pointer-px to device-px conversion. No other module may grow its own variant (FR-26).

Do NOT use AnnotationState.Frozen. It paints an opaque Theme.color.surface fill (AnnotationMark.kt line 98) that would cover the exact device pixels the annotation points at, contradicting its own KDoc. Use Pinned/Selected plus the new scrim. AnnotationState.Frozen remains shipped with no caller in this spec — record that so a later reviewer does not read it as an oversight.

Zero new version-catalog entries, zero new Gradle modules, zero convention-plugin changes. Build per module — the Kotlin daemon is capped at 3 GB, so :presentation-core-ui and :presentation-feature-mirror are built separately, not via a root `build`.
withTimeoutOrNull, never withTimeout, anywhere a timeout is needed.
AC-9 / FR-9 ship at minimum-demo fidelity only — straight Canvas leader lines, nominal popover bounds, no elbow-stagger polish. Explicitly deferred, not silently dropped.

risks.text: Density-trap regression: a future call site converts px to dp by hand instead of going through FrameGeometry, and every annotation anchor silently shifts by 2x on Retina.
risks.mitigation: One pure conversion path (FR-26) built and tested as step 1 before any UI exists; AC-46's fixture reproduces the POC's exact trap; FrameGeometry kept internal so no other module can grow its own variant; a code-review checklist line that any new .dp arithmetic on frame coordinates is a defect.

risks.text: The annotation overlay is drawn in a box that is not pixel-identical to MirrorFrameView's aspect-fit image, producing a constant small offset that no unit test can see.
risks.mitigation: Compose the overlay INSIDE MirrorFrameView's own aspect-fit Box via the new overlay slot, so the overlay literally cannot be a different rectangle. Duplicating the aspectRatio maths in the feature module is explicitly forbidden. Verify once visually at two window sizes and with the side panel at both width bounds.

risks.text: A FocusRequester attached to CommentPopover's root Column may not forward focus to the inner BasicTextField, breaking the autofocus AC-7 requires. VERIFIED: CommentPopover has no focusRequester parameter and its BasicTextField owns a private interactionSource (CommentPopover.kt lines 110-135, 228-235).
risks.mitigation: First try parent FocusRequester + Modifier.focusRequester().focusGroup() on the popover's root. If focus does not land on the field, add `focusRequester: FocusRequester? = null` to CommentPopover and pass it to the BasicTextField — a 3-line, source-compatible, defaulted-parameter kit change. Budgeted in step 8, not a surprise.

risks.text: Making sidePanel non-null activates Cmd+1/2/3 for the first time: handleShellShortcut currently returns false (does not consume) while the panel is absent (RectifyWindow.kt lines 326-330). F-1's shortcut behaviour becomes live in this spec.
risks.mitigation: Expected and desirable — F-1's own comment says the panel is null only because there was no content, which is exactly what this spec fixes. handleShellShortcut is private and untested, and ShortcutToTabTest.kt tests only the pure mapper, so the 160 tests are not mechanically at risk; the exposure is behavioural. Run the full desktop suite immediately after step 9 and call the change out in the PR.

risks.text: A commonTest backtick name containing a comma, apostrophe or colon compiles on the JVM and breaks compileTestKotlinIosArm64. This broke the repo once in F-1 (fixed at a71d232).
risks.mitigation: Plain camelCase test names only, no backticks at all in the five new test files. Run :presentation-feature-mirror:compileTestKotlinIosArm64 and :presentation-core-ui:compileTestKotlinIosArm64 before the PR, not after.

risks.text: AC-47's ViewModel test needs two distinguishable ImageBitmap instances, but MirrorFakes deliberately uses decodeFrame = { null } to keep a graphics backend out of unit tests. Allocating ImageBitmap(w,h) in a headless desktopTest JVM pulls in Skiko's native library.
risks.mitigation: Add a `decodeFrame` parameter to MirrorFakes.mirrorViewModel() (defaulting to the existing null decoder) and a fake decoder that maps byte content to ImageBitmap(width, height) of distinguishing sizes; assert on frozenFrame.value?.width, not on pixel content. ImageBitmap(1080, 2400) is already constructed in commonMain by MirrorFrameViewPreview, so it compiles on every target. FALLBACK if Skiko will not load headless: have the freeze handler also reduce the release-time IntSize into FrozenFrame.deviceSize and assert on that instead — the reducer already stores it, so the assertion moves with zero production change.

risks.text: Keeping the capture loop running while frozen means continuous screencap on the device during what may be minutes of typing.
risks.mitigation: Accepted by FR-30 and already a logged open question. If it bites, the fix is an isFrozen flag folded into the transport's adaptive interval, not a session teardown — setting sessionDeviceId = null would also restart discovery polling and tear the adb session down.

risks.text: The scrim colour is a deliberate literal (always dark in both themes) rather than a Theme token, which design-tokens.md generally forbids.
risks.mitigation: Follows the documented exception pattern already in CommentPopover (PopoverInk, FieldFill) and CounterBadge (Color.White on a signal fill): fixed values with an explicit KDoc rationale because they sit over unknown-brightness device content. One named constant in one file; promote to a ThemeColor token the moment a second call site appears.

risks.text: FR-9's relocation threshold uses nominal popover-bounds constants rather than measured sizes, so a long comment could crowd without triggering relocation.
risks.mitigation: AC-9 is demo-verified, not test-verified. Measuring in order to decide whether to compose is a circular layout dependency that would need SubcomposeLayout — explicitly not worth it at this fidelity. Named constant, one-line tune.

risks.text: Adding MirrorStage.Frozen makes the when(state.stage) in MirrorStageContent non-exhaustive.
risks.mitigation: This is a feature, not a risk: MirrorStage is an enum and the when has no else branch, so the compiler forces the Frozen branch to be written. Step 3 is compile-only and will fail until step 6 lands the branch — sequence them in the same slice or land a `-> Unit` placeholder in step 3.

risks.text: Deleting the last annotation leaves the frame frozen with zero holes, so the scrim degrades to a full-frame dim over a static picture with nothing marked.
risks.mitigation: Accepted as the honest rendering — AC-48 explicitly keeps the stage frozen after Clear, and the Resume Live control stays visible and is the way out. AnnotationOverlay must handle an empty rect list without building a degenerate Path.

functional.text: Support click-and-drag on the live mirror to draw a selection box, rendering a dashed red outline, a live device-pixel size label, and ruler/tick coordinate guides during the drag.
On drag release, freeze the exact current frame and create a new staged annotation anchored to the drawn box.

On a frozen frame, dim everything outside annotation boxes and show a per-annotation popover with a numbered badge, an autofocused free-text comment field (placeholder 'What's wrong here?'), a delete control, and a size/position meta line; Enter saves, clicking the delete control removes the annotation.
When annotation popovers would crowd/overlap, relocate them to a gutter/sidebar panel connected to their boxes via leader lines.

Establish device screenshot pixels as the single canonical storage space for annotation geometry. Implement the pointer-px -> density -> composable-dp -> frame-display-scale -> device-px conversion as one pure, platform-agnostic function (no Composable, no ViewModel side effects) rather than inline per call site, so every caller (the live drag box, the size label, the ruler extent) shares one code path and one set of tests.

Wire the toolbar's stagedCounter slot to the live staged-annotation count (CounterBadgeState.Empty at 0, Staged otherwise) and the clearAction slot to removing every staged annotation while leaving the stage frozen (not ending the session).

Fill the side panel's Notes tab with one AnnotationRow per staged annotation (index, comment or the empty-state copy, position meta line), kept in sync with the same staged-annotation list FR-27 wires to the toolbar; selecting a row selects the corresponding mark on the frame.

Scope annotation keyboard handling to the focused popover: Enter commits the comment text and keeps the annotation pinned; Escape collapses the popover back to a pinned, unselected mark without deleting it; the delete control (CommentPopover's existing close affordance, repurposed to mean delete per FR-8) removes the annotation and decrements the staged count. None of these three consume or bubble into the window-level Cmd+1/2/3 tab shortcut or the device picker's own Escape handler — both already key off disjoint event shapes (meta-modified keys vs. a focus subtree that cannot coexist with the frozen-frame stage).

On freeze, replace the live MirrorFrameView with a static render of the captured bitmap plus a dim/scrim treatment outside every annotation box, retain the device name in the existing toolbar/status chrome, and expose a 'Resume Live' control that discards the frozen frame and its staged annotations and returns the stage to live streaming. Freezing is a display-level snapshot only: the underlying sessionDeviceId-gated capture/transport loop is never paused or restarted, so resuming needs no new adb session.

While a frame is frozen, further drag-and-release gestures on the stage add additional staged annotations against the same frozen frame rather than re-triggering the freeze transition or replacing the captured bitmap.

nonFunctional.text: Live mirror glass-to-glass latency should stay low enough (target under ~150 ms) that drag-to-select and freeze feel responsive.
Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers).
All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given live mirror is streaming, when the user drags on the mirror, then a dashed red outline, live pixel-size label, and ruler guides render in real time.
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: PRD-inherited mismatch: no Compose UI-test harness exists in this repo (zero UI tests among 160 green). Satisfied by FrameGeometryTest (where the box lands) + AnnotationFormatTest (what the size label says) + a light/dark @Preview of the drawing state + a manual demo via ./gradlew :desktop-application:run. The dashed-ness of the border and the Ruler's ticks are verified by preview and demo, not by assertion. 'Adopt compose-ui-test' is raised as its own follow-up ticket, not silently substituted.

acceptanceCriteria.text: When the user releases the drag, then the exact frame is frozen and a new staged annotation is created anchored to the drawn box.
Given a frozen frame with one annotation, then everything outside the box dims and a popover with numbered badge, autofocused comment field, delete control, and meta line appears.
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: Same PRD-inherited test/no-harness mismatch as AC-5. Satisfied by MirrorViewModelAnnotationTest (stage == Frozen with one annotation and selectedIndex set, so the popover is composed) + AnnotationFormatTest (the meta line string) + a light/dark @Preview of AnnotationOverlay and the frozen stage + a manual demo for the dim, the autofocus and the delete affordance.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an annotation popover is focused, when the user presses Enter, then the comment saves; when the user clicks the delete control, then the annotation is removed and the staged count decrements.
Given three annotations are drawn close together, when their popovers would overlap, then they relocate to a sidebar/gutter panel connected via leader lines.
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: The pure overlap predicate IS unit-tested (PopoverCrowdingTest); the relocation rendering and the leader lines are demo-verified. The gutter is the stage's own right edge, not the Notes tab (binding decision 8).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a host density of 2.0 and a known frame display scale, when a drag's raw pointer start/end offsets are converted through the canonical coordinate function, then the resulting device-pixel rect matches the hand-computed expected value (density-trap regression test — the POC's documented 2x offset must not reproduce).

Given the mirror is streaming and MirrorViewModel.frame publishes a new bitmap mid-drag, when the user releases, then the frozen bitmap is the one frame held at release time, not the one held at drag start.

Given N staged annotations, then the toolbar's stagedCounter slot renders CounterBadge(count=N, state=Staged) (or Empty at N=0); clicking the clearAction slot empties the staged list and the badge returns to Empty/0 while the stage remains frozen.
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: The reducer half (list emptied, frozen survives Clear) is unit-tested. The CounterBadge Empty/Staged mapping is a one-expression private helper in RectifyWindow.kt and is inspected, since compose-application has no test source set.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given staged annotations exist, then the side panel's Notes tab renders one AnnotationRow per annotation in index order; clicking a row selects its corresponding mark on the frame (AnnotationState.Selected).
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: The selection reducer (SelectAnnotation sets selectedIndex; the stage maps selectedIndex to AnnotationState.Selected) is unit-tested and the ordering invariant (annotations always index-ordered, indices recomputed after delete) is unit-tested. One-row-per-annotation rendering is inspected in the Notes tab preview and the demo.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an annotation popover has focus, pressing Escape collapses only that popover (keeping the annotation pinned, count unchanged) without affecting the device picker or the active side-panel tab; Cmd+1/2/3 still switches side-panel tabs while a popover is focused.
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: The reducer half (SelectAnnotation(null) keeps the annotation and the count) is unit-tested. The non-interference half is argued structurally and demo-verified: handleShellShortcut matches only isMetaPressed (RectifyWindow.kt line 327 via shortcutToTab), and MirrorStage.Picker and MirrorStage.Frozen are mutually exclusive enum values so the picker's focus subtree cannot coexist with the popover's. ShortcutToTabTest.kt already covers the meta-only mapping.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a frame is frozen with staged annotations, when the user activates the Resume Live control, then the stage returns to the live mirror and the staged annotation list is cleared; a subsequent drag freezes a new frame.
acceptanceCriteria.verificationNote: The reducer half (ResumeLive nulls frozen and frozenFrame; stage returns to Mirror; a following StageAnnotation freezes again) IS unit-tested even though the AC is marked demo — the demo covers the perceptual half, that live frames resume with no reconnection stall.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a frame is already frozen with one staged annotation, when the user drags and releases again on the stage, then a second staged annotation is added against the same frozen frame without re-triggering the freeze transition.

architecture.approach: Extend presentation-feature-mirror in place across four layers — pure geometry, Orbit state, a render-only freeze, and assembled UI — plus two source-compatible defaulted parameters and one new molecule in presentation-core-ui, and a call-site rewiring in compose-application's RectifyWindow.kt. No new Gradle module, no new Koin module, no persistence, no serialization.
architecture.rationale: Every visual element the input artifact called unillustrated already exists as a shipped, previewed kit component except the dim-outside-boxes scrim, which is small enough to author as one molecule now. This matches the 'assemble, don't author' norm F-1 and F-2 both independently reached. The coordinate conversion is isolated into one pure internal function because an off-by-density bug there silently corrupts every annotation anchor and no other test would catch it; device screenshot pixels is the canonical storage space because it is resolution- and window-stable and is exactly what FR-6's label, Ruler's extentPx and F-7's eventual payload all need. Freeze-at-release rather than at drag start, because FR-6 frames the drag as happening live, so 'the exact current frame' reads as current-at-release — and reading MirrorViewModel.frame's latest value once inside the release handler needs no buffering, which makes AC-47 true by construction. Annotations go into the Orbit reduced state, the opposite of frames, because they are small, value-equal, mutated a handful of times per session and read by three simultaneous consumers — exactly the shape reduced state exists for — whereas frames are identity-compared blobs arriving ten times a second. A new presentation-feature-annotation module was rejected: it would need the live frame StateFlow and the stage state from MirrorViewModel, and two ViewModels sharing a bitmap stream is worse coupling than one class with six more handlers, on top of a new convention-plugin wiring and a load-order-significant initKoin entry for a split that F-5..F-8 have not yet justified.

alternativesConsidered.title: Inline coordinate conversion per call site, POC-style
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Three call sites (drag box, size label, ruler extent) would each have to get density right independently, and the POC shape is exactly what produced the documented 2x offset. It is also untestable without a display. This is the one place in the spec where laziness buys a silent data-corruption bug.

alternativesConsidered.title: Store annotations in composable dp and convert only at send time (F-7's job)
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: dp is not resolution-stable across an aspect-fit frame — the stored value breaks the moment the window or the side panel is resized, which the shell supports as a first-class interaction.

alternativesConsidered.title: Put the frozen ImageBitmap into MirrorUiState alongside the annotations
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Violates presentation-feature-mirror's documented deviation 2: a ByteArray-bearing type compares by identity and could never deduplicate in the reducer. The bitmap goes on a second StateFlow beside frame; the reducer stores only its IntSize, which is all the meta lines, the Ruler extent and FrameGeometry actually need.

alternativesConsidered.title: A new presentation-feature-annotation Gradle module
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Needs the live frame StateFlow and the stage state from MirrorViewModel; two ViewModels sharing a bitmap stream is worse coupling than one class with six more handlers. Also costs a new convention-plugin wiring, a new Koin module and a load-order-significant initKoin entry, for a split F-5/F-6/F-7/F-8 have not landed to justify. When F-7 needs StagedAnnotation in a payload, lift the MODEL to domain-core — a 20-line move that needs no module today.

alternativesConsidered.title: Pause the capture/transport loop while frozen
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Pausing means setting sessionDeviceId = null, which also restarts discovery polling and tears the adb session down — a far bigger behavioural change than the power it saves, and it would put a reconnection stall in front of Resume Live. Explicitly accepted by FR-30 and recorded as a deferred optimisation.

alternativesConsidered.title: Use AnnotationState.Frozen for frozen-frame marks
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: AnnotationMark.kt line 98 fills the mark with an opaque Theme.color.surface in that state, covering the exact device pixels the annotation points at — it would hide the bug the user is reporting. Pinned/Selected plus the new scrim needs no kit change. Binding decision 7.

alternativesConsidered.title: Scrim as an even-odd hole path, as four rects around each box, or via BlendMode.Clear in a saveLayer
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: An even-odd path XORs overlapping holes and would re-dim their intersection; four-rects-per-box is simply wrong with two or more boxes; BlendMode.Clear needs a saveLayer, allocating a full-frame offscreen Skia surface every draw. clipPath(ClipOp.Difference) + one drawRect is a single path fill that unions overlapping holes correctly and never touches the ImageBitmap.

alternativesConsidered.title: FR-9's gutter inside the Notes tab, as the clarify gate literally worded it
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: FR-28 already fills the Notes tab with one AnnotationRow per annotation, so every annotation would render twice in the same panel, and each leader line would have to cross from the stage over the resize handle into a separately-composed panel via onGloballyPositioned window coordinates. It also silently breaks when the user hides the side panel. Binding decision 8 revises this to an in-stage right-edge gutter where the mark and the line live in one coordinate space.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add compose-ui-test (desktop) in this spec and write real rendering assertions for AC-5/AC-7
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: That is a cross-cutting decision about the project's whole testing strategy, landing a new test dependency in every module through the convention plugins. It deserves its own spec. Nearly all the real risk in AC-5/AC-7 — where the box lands, what the label says, which marks exist — is pure and is covered here; what a renderer would add is 'the dashed border is dashed', which a preview shows faster. Raised as a follow-up ticket.

alternativesConsidered.title: Author a second VerticalRuler kit component for FR-6's vertical guide
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Ruler's own KDoc rules it out: 'the vertical ruler in the reference is the same strip rotated by the host, and duplicating the tick maths for it would buy nothing.' The host rotates the existing Ruler in a fixed-size Box with swapped dimensions.

alternativesConsidered.title: Change MirrorHost's and MirrorStageContent's signatures to carry both the live and the frozen bitmap
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Two positional nullable ImageBitmaps is a footgun, and it would churn RectifyShellContent's parameter list and every existing call site. MirrorHost instead computes displayFrame = frozenFrame ?: frame internally; the fallback is unreachable because StageAnnotation is dropped when frame is null, so frozen != null implies a non-null bitmap.

interfaces.name: FrameGeometry.toDevice
interfaces.contract: (start: Offset, end: Offset) -> IntRect. Pure. Normalises a reversed drag to a positive rect, converts via devicePx = pointerPx / framePx * deviceSize with NO density term, rounds each corner independently, clamps into 0..deviceSize on both axes. Returns IntRect.Zero when framePx has a zero dimension.

interfaces.name: FrameGeometry.toFrame
interfaces.contract: (rect: IntRect) -> Rect. Pure. Device px back to frame-local px for rendering. Inverse of toDevice up to rounding.

interfaces.name: FrameGeometry.toDp
interfaces.contract: (rect: Rect) -> DpRect. Pure. Frame px to dp by dividing by density. The single place in the entire feature where density appears.

interfaces.name: FrameGeometry.isMeaningfulDrag
interfaces.contract: (rect: IntRect) -> Boolean. True when both width and height are at least MIN_DRAG_DEVICE_PX (8). Guards the worst accidental interaction in a live-mirroring tool: a stray click freezing the mirror.

architecture.stateManagement: Orbit MVI in presentation-feature-mirror, four-file convention, existing container. Three tiers by mutation frequency: (1) transient drag offsets live in composable `remember` and never reach Orbit — a pointer move at 60 Hz through the reducer is the mistake F-2 avoided for frames; (2) pixel blobs (the live frame and now the frozen frame) live on plain StateFlows outside the reducer, preserving the module's documented deviation 2; (3) semantic state (the staged annotation list, the selected index, the frozen frame's IntSize) lives in MirrorUiState because it is small, value-equal, mutated a handful of times per session and read simultaneously by the toolbar badge, the Notes tab and the stage marks. MirrorStage.Frozen is derived from `frozen != null` in the existing stage getter, so no second flag exists to fall out of sync. The frozen bitmap and the frozen reduced state are set inside the same intent, and the render path falls back to the live frame if the bitmap were ever null — one `?:`, no sync machinery.
navigation: None. presentation-feature-mirror has no Destination and will not get one — it is a set of shell slots the desktop window fills, as its module CLAUDE.md documents (deviation 1). The five-step checklist in .claude/rules/navigation.md is deliberately not applied: no Destination case, no navSavedStateConfiguration entry, no NavigationHost branch.

The only navigation-like change is within the shell: Cmd+1/2/3 side-panel tab switching becomes live for the first time because the panel slot stops being null, and the first annotation of a frozen frame auto-selects the Notes tab.

errorStates.behavior: Frozen frame with zero annotations (after Clear, or after deleting the last one): the stage stays frozen per AC-48, the scrim degrades to a plain full-frame dim because the hole list is empty, and the Resume Live control stays visible as the way out. AnnotationOverlay must not build a degenerate Path from an empty list.

Notes tab with zero annotations: renders one muted line of empty-state copy (mirror_annotation_notes_empty), never a blank panel. The tab count renders as absent rather than 0 so SidebarTabs does not show a meaningless zero.
Annotation with no comment yet: AnnotationRow renders its empty-state copy rather than collapsing, because the mark still exists on the frame and the user needs a way back to it.
Frame box size is 0 on first composition, before onSizeChanged reports: FrameGeometry returns an empty rect and the drag layer composes nothing rather than dividing by zero.

Session started but no frame decoded yet (frame == null on the Mirror stage): unchanged F-2 behaviour, the stage's dot grid shows. A drag release in this state drops the StageAnnotation intent and the stage stays live — nothing to freeze.

Sub-minimum drag (a click, or under MIN_DRAG_DEVICE_PX in either axis): discarded silently — no annotation, no freeze. Without this a stray click on the stage freezes the mirror, the worst accidental interaction in a live-mirroring tool.

Drag starting inside the frame and ending in the letterbox, or a reversed right-to-left / bottom-to-top drag: toDevice normalises to a positive rect and clamps into device bounds, so the stored rect is never negative and never past width/height.

Delete of the currently selected annotation: selectedIndex is recomputed — clamped into the new range or nulled — never left dangling at a removed index, and the remaining annotations' indices are renumbered so the badges stay 1..N.

MirrorSession.Lost while frozen: the frozen frame and its annotations are KEPT. The user is mid-sentence and a device dying must not erase their work. The status indicator stays Frozen; Resume Live then lands on NoSignal.

Platform switched to iOS, or StopMirroring, while frozen: selectPlatform/stopSession already null the session and must also null both the frozen state and the frozen bitmap, or a stale Android frame would sit under the iOS notice.

An annotation drawn at the extreme right or bottom edge: the CommentPopover (min 300 dp wide) would overflow the stage, so its x is clamped into the stage bounds. Its tail has a fixed 18 dp inset and will not follow — a known demo-fidelity limitation whose eventual fix is a tailOffset parameter.
Escape pressed with no popover focused: falls through untouched. The device picker's own Escape handler and the shell must still behave (AC-50).

logs: No new Kermit logger is introduced in presentation-feature-mirror — it has none today and a reducer that logs every annotation would be noise. The existing RectifyWindow logger keeps its warnings.

One exception worth considering at review time only: a single Logger.w when StageAnnotation is dropped because frame == null, since that is the one silent discard a user could report as 'the drag did nothing'. Deferred unless review asks for it.
metrics: No new metric. The existing MirrorStatsModel line (tool version, frame dimensions, fps) keeps rendering while frozen, which is itself the honest signal that the capture loop was never paused.
analyticsEvents: None. This project ships no analytics pipeline and this spec does not introduce one.

accessibility.requirement: NFR-8: the comment popover is fully keyboard operable — Enter commits the comment and keeps the annotation pinned, Escape collapses the popover to a pinned unselected mark without deleting it. Both are handled by onPreviewKeyEvent on the popover's own focus subtree, the pattern DevicePickerPanel already established.

The popover's comment field receives focus automatically when an annotation is created or selected, so the user can type immediately without reaching for the pointer (AC-7). If parent-delegated focus does not reach the BasicTextField, CommentPopover gains a defaulted focusRequester parameter.

Enter and Escape in the popover must not consume or bubble into the window-level Cmd+1/2/3 shortcut, and Cmd+1/2/3 must keep switching tabs while a comment field has focus. The event shapes are disjoint (handleShellShortcut matches only isMetaPressed) and the stages are mutually exclusive, so no new dispatch layer is added (AC-50).
Typing a bare digit into the comment field must never switch side-panel tabs — the same isMetaPressed disjointness. Explicitly walked through in the demo.

The delete control is a real Role.Button with a content description (CommentPopover's CloseButton already is), and the Resume Live control is an AppButton with visible text rather than an icon-only affordance.

MirrorFrameView's existing semantics contentDescription naming the mirrored device is preserved when the overlay slot is added — the overlay is composed inside that Box and must not replace or clear its semantics.

NFR-9: light and dark parity for every new surface. The scrim and the popovers are deliberately dark in BOTH themes (they sit over unknown-brightness device content), which is the documented exception pattern, not a parity failure — the mark borders, the badges, the Notes rows and the Resume Live button all follow the theme and are checked in both.

Annotation state is never signalled by colour alone: every mark carries a numbered GlyphBadge and every Notes row repeats that number, so the frame and the sidebar stay cross-referenceable without colour discrimination.

performanceBudget.metric: Scrim + overlay draw cost over a live-sized frame
performanceBudget.target: One Canvas, one Path built from at most ~10 rects, one clipPath(ClipOp.Difference) and one drawRect per draw. NO saveLayer, NO offscreen Skia surface, and the ImageBitmap is never read, copied or composited. Budget: at most one extra full-frame-box fill per draw pass — the frame box is the aspect-fit display rectangle (roughly 713x1584 px at the default window on a 1080x2400 device), not the 1080x2400 source bitmap.
O(n) in the number of annotations, n <= ~10 in practice. Build the union Path inside remember(rects) so a pointer move or a recomposition that does not change the rect list does not rebuild it.

The drawn box follows the pointer within one frame (<= 16 ms at 60 Hz). Achieved by keeping dragStart/dragCurrent in composable remember so a pointer move recomposes only the overlay subtree and never passes through the Orbit reducer.
Exactly one (the StageAnnotation on release). Zero during the drag. This is the invariant that keeps a 60 Hz gesture from becoming 60 state copies a second, mirroring F-2's frame decision.

Unchanged at under ~150 ms. Freeze is render-only — sessionDeviceId and the flatMapLatest gate are untouched — so the capture/decode/transport path has exactly the same cost before, during and after a freeze.

First live frame visible within one capture interval (~100 ms at the current cadence), with no adb reconnection. This is the whole payoff of the render-only freeze and is the headline thing the SC-11 demo checks.

No per-frame work on the stage while frozen — the static bitmap and the scrim redraw only on recomposition, not on each arriving capture. Accepted cost: the device keeps running screencap behind a static picture (FR-30), logged as a deferred optimisation whose fix would be an isFrozen flag in the transport's adaptive interval, not a session teardown.
O(n^2) pairwise over n <= ~10 nominal rects, recomputed only when the annotation list or the frame box changes — well under a microsecond and explicitly not worth a sweep-line.
At most one extra ImageBitmap alive at a time (the frozen frame), released on Resume Live, platform switch or StopMirroring. No history, no buffering, no serialization (AS-11).
Roughly 900 added lines or fewer across all four modules. Exceeding that means the reuse-first premise has failed and the plan should be revisited rather than the budget raised.

i18n.notes: presentation-core-ui must not depend on presentation-core-localisation, so AnnotationOverlay and every other kit-level change takes copy as a parameter with an English default and the feature module supplies stringResource(). Machine output — the device-pixel size label and the `218×77 @ 1035,862` meta line — is rendered mono and deliberately carries no resource key, matching how serials, versions and fps are already handled. RectifyWindow.kt's existing literal labels (Clear, Resolve & Send, No device, staged) stay literal: that is F-1's established pattern for that file and converting them is out-of-scope churn for this spec; it should be its own small ticket.

dataHandling: Annotations are held in memory only. No disk write, no serialization, no new data module, no file I/O — the POC's JSON writer is F-7's and F-8's business (AS-11).
The frozen bitmap is a reference to an already-decoded in-memory frame. Nothing new is captured, copied to disk or transmitted.
Comment text is free user input but never reaches a shell command, a file path or a network call in this spec. It is rendered and held, nothing more.
permissions: No new OS permission, no new adb capability, no new process invocation. The capture loop this spec rides on is F-2's and is unchanged.
privacy: SEC-1 stays closed. Frame dimensions are read from the decoded ImageBitmap, never from GetProp. F-2 left GetProp with zero production callers and NFR-5 holds there only by that absence; this spec creates no new caller — a grep for GetProp must still return zero production hits after this lands.
No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporting: a device screenshot and a bug note never leave the host in this deliverable.

rollout.backwardCompatibility: Every kit API change is a defaulted parameter added at the end of the parameter list (MirrorFrameView.overlay, RectifyWindowShell.tabCounts, contingently CommentPopover.focusRequester), so every existing call site, preview and test compiles unchanged. MirrorHost's and MirrorStageContent's public signatures do not change at all. Two user-visible behaviour changes DO land and must be called out in the PR: (1) Cmd+1/2/3 side-panel tab switching becomes live for the first time, because handleShellShortcut only consumed the event while a panel was on screen and the panel was always null; (2) the side panel is now composed permanently rather than never, so the window layout differs from F-1's shipped appearance from the first frame. Both are intended — F-1's own code comment says the panel was null only because there was no content to put in it, which is precisely what this spec supplies. MirrorStage gaining a Frozen enum entry is a source-compatible change inside the feature module, and the compiler enforces the new when branch rather than letting it be forgotten.

openQuestions: Whether to pause the capture/transport loop while frozen (power/perf optimisation) is left for later — FR-30 assumes it keeps running. If it bites, the fix is an isFrozen flag folded into the transport's adaptive interval, not a session teardown.
The gutter/leader-line 8 px elbow-stagger visual polish named in AnnotationPopover's KDoc is not implemented in v1 — a follow-up design/visual-QA pass should revisit it.
Whether a frozen frame should ever be allowed to persist annotations across a Resume-Live -> freeze-again cycle (multi-frame annotation sets) is explicitly deferred to F-8 (history).

Vertical ruler for FR-6's 'ruler/tick guides': this plan takes the recommendation — horizontal plus vertical via the existing Ruler rotated 270 degrees in a fixed-size Box, as the component's own KDoc anticipates, rather than authoring a second VerticalRuler. The rotation wrapper does not exist yet and is built in step 6; if rotation produces an unacceptable tick-label orientation, the fallback is horizontal-only, which still satisfies FR-6's wording.

Where the Resume Live control sits: this plan takes the recommendation — a stage top-right overlay AppButton over the scrim, because the toolbar's primaryAction is reserved for F-7's 'Resolve & Send' and the status bar is only 28 dp tall. The geometry constant is flagged for design review.

Minimum drag size before an annotation is created: this plan takes the recommendation — a named MIN_DRAG_DEVICE_PX constant at 8 device px in both axes. The exact value is a one-line tune and is flagged for review after the first real session.

Does the Notes tab auto-activate on first freeze: this plan takes the recommendation — auto-select Notes on the FIRST annotation of a frozen frame only, never on subsequent ones, so a user who deliberately switched to Payload is not fought. Implemented in RectifyWindow because ShellState.activeTab has a private setter.

No design comp exists for ANY part of this feature — the scrim alpha, the Resume Live placement and geometry, the ruler placement, the gutter width and the leader-line routing are all invented. Every one ships as a named private constant so the later design conversation is a one-line change each (precedent: F-1's stage dot grid).

CommentPopover's X affordance means DELETE here (FR-8) while Escape means COLLAPSE (FR-29) — two visually similar dismissals with different destructiveness and no confirm. No design input exists on how to visually differentiate them; shipped as-is and flagged.

CommentPopover's tail has a fixed 18 dp inset and no placement logic, so a popover clamped away from its mark's edge will point at the wrong place. Accepted at demo fidelity — a tailOffset parameter is the eventual fix.

StagedAnnotation lives in the presentation contract for now (one consumer, no serialization need); lift it to domain-core only when F-7 needs it in an MCP payload — that is a package move, not a redesign.

NEW (plan): making the side panel permanently composed changes the window's appearance from the first frame and activates Cmd+1/2/3 for the first time. This plan chooses permanent over session-gated because the alternative needs the mirror state inside the Window's onPreviewKeyEvent, where it is not available without a composition-time side effect. If a session-gated panel is wanted, it is a separate small refactor of how isPanelVisible is hoisted.
